lines.text: How does this cell leave your blood? This wall has no open door.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ dˈʌz ðɪs sˈɛl lˈiːv jɔː blˈʌd? ðɪs wˈɔːl hɐz nˈəʊ ˈəʊpən dˈɔː.

lines.text: It's a neutrophil, your commonest white cell, about eight micrometres across. Yet under a sore fingertip, they pile up outside the wall.
lines.phonemes: ɪts ɐ njˈuːtɹəfˌɪl, jɔː kˈɒmənɪst wˈaɪt sˈɛl, ɐbˌaʊt ˈeɪt mˈaɪkɹəʊmˌiːtəz əkɹˈɒs. jˈɛt ˌʌndəɹ ɐ sˈɔː fˈɪŋɡətˌɪp, ðeɪ pˈaɪl ˌʌp aʊtsˈaɪd ðə wˈɔːl.

lines.text: Rudolf Virchow taught that pus grew from the inflamed tissue. In eighteen sixty-seven, his assistant Julius Cohnheim watched a living frog's vessels. White cells climbed out.
lines.phonemes: ɹˈuːdɒlf fˈɪəkəʊ tˈɔːt ðat pˈʌs ɡɹˈuː fɹʌmðɪ ɪnflˈeɪmd tˈɪʃuː. ɪn ˈeɪtiːn sˈɪkstisˈɛvən, hɪz ɐsˈɪstənt dʒˈuːlɪəs kˈəʊnhaɪm wˈɒtʃt ɐ lˈɪvɪŋ fɹˈɒɡz vˈɛsəlz. wˈaɪt sˈɛlz klˈaɪmd ˈaʊt.

lines.text: Where tissue is inflamed, the wall turns sticky, and the cell rolls. Then its grips switch on, and it stops. It crawls to a seam between two wall cells. In a rare inherited condition, those grips are faulty. Cells roll on past.
lines.phonemes: wˌeə tˈɪʃuː ɪz ɪnflˈeɪmd, ðə wˈɔːl tˈɜːnz stˈɪki, and ðə sˈɛl ɹˈəʊlz. ðˈɛn ɪts ɡɹˈɪps swˈɪtʃ ˈɒn, and ɪt stˈɒps. ɪt kɹˈɔːlz tʊ ɐ sˈiːm bɪtwˌiːn tˈuː wˈɔːl sˈɛlz. ɪn ɐ ɹˈeəɹ ɪnhˈɛɹɪtɪd kəndˈɪʃən, ðəʊz ɡɹˈɪps ɑː fˈɒlti. sˈɛlz ɹˈəʊl ˈɒn pˈɑːst .

lines.text: This one wedges its nucleus into the seam, making its own door. It pours through a gap narrower than itself. Behind it, the seam seals shut.
lines.phonemes: ðˈɪswˌɒn wˈɛdʒɪz ɪts njˈuːklɪəs ˌɪntʊ ðə sˈiːm, mˌeɪkɪŋ ɪts ˈəʊn dˈɔː. ɪt pˈɔːz θɹuː ɐ ɡˈap nˈaɹəʊə ðɐn ɪtsˈɛlf. bɪhˈaɪnd ɪt, ðə sˈiːm sˈiːlz ʃˈʌt.

lines.text: So pus is mostly white cells from your blood. Each one let itself out.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ pˈʌs ɪz mˈəʊstli wˈaɪt sˈɛlz fɹɒm jɔː blˈʌd. ˈiːtʃ wˈɒn lˈɛt ɪtsˈɛlf ˈaʊt.

lines.text: Meanwhile, as you watched, your bone marrow made new neutrophils. More than ten million.
lines.phonemes: mˈiːnwaɪl, az juː wˈɒtʃt, jɔː bˈəʊn mˈaɹəʊ mˌeɪd njˈuː njˈuːtɹəfˌɪlz. mˈɔː ðɐn tˈɛn mˈɪliən.

lines.text: Next: the spark. What sets off nearly every heartbeat you have?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: ðə spˈɑːk. wˌɒt sˈɛts ˈɒf nˌiəli ˈɛvɹɪ hˈɑːtbiːt juː hˈav?
